message.content:
Review: The problem is clearly scoped as a follow-up to the identified study, and it correctly distinguishes the published claim from what the supplied aggregate export can establish. The proposed experiment targets an important causal ambiguity: changing coupling may alter temporal order directly or through dynamics other than spatial coarsening. Randomized repeated runs, synchronized unit-level data, prespecified measures, and run-level uncertainty make the central comparison testable. The supplied data alone are insufficient for that test; new experiments and access to raw motion and drive signals are essential.

Feedback: Feasibility is good for testing whether coupling conditions change coarsening and subharmonic order in this array, assuming the coupling is controllable and unit-level signals can be measured reliably. The main challenges are experimental repeatability, sufficient independent runs, and validating the spectral estimator and onset threshold against noise, finite windows, and drive-frequency drift. Censoring runs without onset is appropriate, but the analysis should also account for uncertainty in onset times and any dependence among runs or units. A drive-only comparison can help identify direct drive responses, though it may not isolate every alternative pathway. Most importantly, association between correlation length and onset, even across conditions, will not by itself establish mediation; causal claims should remain limited unless the design can separately manipulate coarsening or otherwise identify that pathway. Generalization beyond this array would require further experiments.

Rating (1-5): 4
